verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts check out exactly and the base-quarter logic is sound, but the size does not reach the print. Amazon Q2 2026 Physical stores was $5,794mm vs $5,595mm (+3.56%) and Q1 2026 was $5,785mm vs $5,533mm (+4.55%) -- so the deceleration is real, and it was visible in Amazon's OWN rounded labels, which went from '5%' in the Q1 release to '4%' in the Q2 release, published 2026-07-30 in the document every Amazon analyst reads and tracked publicly as a series on Statista. Three problems. (1) 'Physical stores' is not Whole Foods: it bundles Amazon Fresh and Amazon Go, and it is retail sell-through, not UNFI's wholesale shipments into the account. (2) Amazon's Apr-Jun quarter covers only two of the three months in UNFI's 13 weeks to 2026-08-01. (3) The arithmetic: 100bp on a customer worth ~20-22% of UNFI net sales is ~20bp of UNFI revenue, about $15mm on a $7.6bn quarter, and at UNFI's ~2.2% adjusted EBITDA margin that is a rounding error against a $0.62 EPS bar. Worse for the hunter, the conclusion it supports -- soft top line -- is already marked: UNFI's revenue line is dominated by its own deliberate network-optimization exits and a single-customer project unwind that management said on 2026-06-09 will 'fully cycle in the third quarter of fiscal 2027', the June print missed revenue by ~$236mm and cost 10.3%, and Q4 consensus revenue of $7.6bn already sits at the very floor of the band implied by guidance (which is UNFI-h2#2's own finding). The sell-side has already taken revenue to the bottom; this datum tells it to do what it has done.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Amazon Q2 2026 Physical stores net sales $5,794mm vs $5,595mm, labelled 4% Y/Y growth including and excluding F/X.
Amazon Q1 2026 Physical stores net sales $5,785mm, labelled 5% Y/Y growth -- so the step down to 4% was disclosed by Amazon itself.
The Amazon physical-store net sales series through Q1/Q2 2026 is published and tracked quarter by quarter.
UNFI management already told the market the revenue headwind is network optimization plus a single-customer project unwind that fully cycles in Q3 FY2027.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Amazon reported on 2026-07-30; UNFI's 20-day run-up is -6.6% and the stock is 20.9% below its 52-week high, so soft top line is not a fresh idea to this tape. The 2026-06-09 reaction of -10.28% was itself a revenue miss, which is when the market re-based UNFI's revenue expectations.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosure that UNFI's shipments to Amazon/Whole Foods specifically fell in the quarter, or evidence that the account is materially larger than the ~20-22% of net sales in the filings, which would move this from a rounding error to a real number.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is two facts welded together and they price completely differently. The reshuffle itself is not obscure at all: the 8-K (report date 2026-07-07) came with a Businesswire press release on 2026-07-09 -- 'United Natural Foods Announces Leadership Updates to Accelerate Value Creation Strategy' -- naming Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10, Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer and Bushway's exit, and it was picked up by TipRanks, The Shelby Report, Supermarket News, Progressive Grocer, Mass Market Retailers, Abasto and Distribution Strategy Group inside 48 hours. Nobody discovers on 2026-09-04 that UNFI has a five-week-old CFO. The Echols Form 4 I concede: I searched and found no press release, no Item 5.02, no trade-press item, and the filing itself does carry the remark that he ceased to be Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24. But that is a communications and public-affairs role with no P&L line and no guidance role -- its earnings content is approximately zero, and it is doing all the work of making this finding look unpublished. Strip it out and what remains is 'a new CFO may sandbag his first guide', which is one of the most widely rehearsed patterns in the market and whose trigger date has been public for eight weeks. The 'day 29' framing is a re-description of a known start date, not a new fact.

prior_publication.what_it_says: UNFI press-released the entire leadership reorganisation, including Luchini as CFO effective 2026-08-10 and Tarditi's move to President/COO.
Aggregator coverage of the same reorganisation on the day of the release.
Trade-press coverage naming Tarditi President/COO and the wider realignment.
Confirmed: Matthew T Echols' Form 4 carries the remark that he no longer serves as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24 -- and I found no other publication of this anywhere.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No isolable move on 2026-07-09 or 2026-08-27 is identifiable from the daily series in the baseline, but the 12.02% implied move with no 25-delta skew means the market states magnitude and no direction -- there is no downside skew bid that would corroborate a governance-churn fear, and equally nothing that contradicts it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Echols' exit was for cause, or that a sixth unannounced departure sits in an operating or finance role that touches guidance, would turn a comms-role footnote into a governance signal.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts are right but the hunter has double-counted the benefit, and every component comes from two documents the company published itself and the hunter itself cites. Verified from the Q3 FY26 release: '$20 million and $40 million of insurance recoveries' in Q3 and YTD, 'included within Operating expenses', the ~$330mm FCF guide, and the cybersecurity reconciliation. But the same release states the $40mm of recoveries is offset by '$22 million of costs and charges' -- which is precisely why the reconciliation line is ($18mm) and not ($40mm). So the one-off flattering FY26 free cash flow is ~$18mm net, roughly 5.5% of the $330mm guide, not the 'at least $40mm' the finding asserts. Against the December 2025 framework, the FY26 guide is $30mm above the ~$300mm anchor and ~$18mm of that is the net cyber item -- a real quality-of-cash-flow point, but worth well under 1% of a $2.67bn market cap. And the framework itself is the problem for the finding: 'Approximately $300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028' is *published guidance* from the 2025-12-10 investor day press release, so if UNFI guides FY27 FCF to ~$300mm on 2026-09-08 that is management restating its own plan on schedule, which is the definition of already priced. The finding is only news if the market thought $330mm was the new run rate, and the company's own published framework says otherwise.

Investor day targets published verbatim, including 'Approximately $300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028' free cash flow.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Both documents predate the last print (2026-06-09, on which the stock fell 10.28% and the guide was only narrowed, not raised). Nothing in the 5-day (-4.1%) or 20-day (-6.6%) tape is attributable to a cash-flow-quality revelation.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: An FY27 FCF guide materially below ~$300mm, or disclosure that a further large insurance recovery landed in Q4 and is inside the ~$330mm, would make the FY26 base look considerably more inflated than $18mm.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This one is in the wire copy and it is arithmetically trivial. Amendment No. 5 was 8-K'd and then written up on the day by Investing.com, TradingView, TipRanks and StockTitan, all of which carried the exact detail the finding leads with -- SOFR margin 4.75% to 4.00% on approximately $371mm, other material terms unchanged. Size: 75bp on $371mm is $2.78mm a year pretax, call it $2.1mm after tax, which on 60.7mm shares outstanding is about $0.035 of annual EPS and under a cent in the quarter being reported. Against a stock at $43.94 with a 12.02% implied move that is roughly a tenth of a point of value, not a thesis. The 'no covenant relief was needed' inference is also weaker than it reads: 2026 has been a broad repricing market and a lender repricing a $371mm first-lien tranche at 2.5x net leverage tells you about loan-market technicals as much as about UNFI. Decisively, the price did not agree that this mattered: the amendment was dated 2026-06-18 and disclosed 2026-06-22, and UNFI has since gone from $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94, with a -6.6% 20-day run-up. A credit-confidence signal that leaves no trace in the equity for eleven weeks is not an unpriced 12%-move catalyst.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Disclosed 2026-06-22 and the stock is lower now than then; no repricing bid is visible in the option chain either (put/call OI ratio 0.54 on only 1,765 contracts, no 25d skew computable).
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the Q4 release paired this with a large debt paydown or a leverage target reset below 2.5x, the credit story would become a re-rating argument rather than a $0.035 EPS item.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I checked the transcript and the quotes are exact -- CFO Dirk Locascio, recovery 'more like 70% for the quarter' against 'our typical 30%, 40%', an expected 'about a 2% headwind from fuel' coming in at 'less than half of that', explicitly because surcharges for larger customers that only activate at elevated prices went into effect. UNFI's own 2026-06-09 language is also exact: hedging, 'contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers', route optimisation. So the mechanism is real and I have not found the read-across written down for UNFI anywhere. That is a genuine concession. The case against it is about transfer and about how much room is left. Transfer: US Foods is broadline foodservice, small drop sizes, a fragmented restaurant base and its own negotiated surcharge tables; UNFI is grocery wholesale whose single largest customer is ~20-22% of net sales and has more negotiating leverage than any USFD account, and UNFI's own word is 'some', not 'most'. Overlap: USFD's quarter is Apr-Jun, UNFI's is 3 May to 1 Aug, and diesel collapsed to $4.58 on 2026-07-06 before rebounding through July -- so the very tiers that fired in May and June may have deactivated in the month USFD does not cover. Room left: UNFI told the market on 2026-06-09 that incremental fuel and transportation costs were already embedded in Q4 guidance, the 2026-09-03 preview repeats it, and Q4 consensus EPS of $0.62 against Q3's $0.77 actual already books a sharp sequential step down that is largely fuel. The upside is therefore against a bar that has already been lowered. What keeps my number low anyway is that the tape moved the other way: UNFI was $47.90 on 2026-08-13, the day of the USFD call, and is $43.94 now -- the market spent those three weeks pricing fuel pain, not surcharge relief.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Locascio's 70%-vs-30/40% recovery rate and the fuel headwind coming in at less than half of the expected 2%, attributed to tiered customer surcharges activating at elevated prices.
Wire coverage of the USFD print framed explicitly around elevated fuel costs and a reaffirmed outlook.
UNFI's three fuel tools including 'contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers', and incremental fuel embedded in Q4 guidance.
Preview copy already states 'incremental fuel and transportation costs factored into fourth-quarter expectations', with no mention of surcharge recovery upside.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The strongest evidence FOR this finding: UNFI fell from $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94 on 2026-09-04 (-8.3%) through exactly the window in which diesel set record August highs, so the tape has priced the fuel headwind and not the offset. No 25d skew is available to check whether puts are bid, and total front-expiry open interest is only 1,765 contracts with a 39%-of-mid ATM spread, so the chain cannot arbitrate direction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A sell-side note or press piece between 2026-08-13 and the print applying USFD's surcharge-recovery beat to UNFI, or disclosure that UNFI's tiered surcharges are capped or waived for its largest account, would take this to 70 or to 5 respectively.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The core mechanic checks out and the precedent is real, which is why my number is not higher: the $200mm programme was approved 2022-09-21 'over four years', so it does lapse this month, and it was itself announced alongside the Q4 FY2022 print on 2022-09-27 -- so a Q4 print is exactly where UNFI re-ups. The $109mm is also credible: $138mm remained at FY23 year end and FY26 year-to-date buybacks were about $38mm at an average of $37.88 per the Q3 call, leaving roughly $100mm. Three things cut it down. First, the theme is already on the record: management said on the 2026-06-09 call it would 'continue to evaluate further opportunistic repurchases as we reinvest in our business and reduce leverage', so buyback capacity is not a discovery. Second, one of the finding's specifics is wrong -- the last buys were not 'struck at $33.66 (Q2)'. The Q3 10-Q shows 0.1mm shares for $4mm in the third quarter, about $40 a share, and the call gives a $37.88 year-to-date average, so buying continued into Q3 well above $33.66, which weakens the 'they only buy when it is cheap, so $43.94 is above their revealed bid' subtext considerably. Third, an authorisation is not a purchase: a board can let a term lapse silently, and UNFI's stated capital priority is deleveraging toward and through 2.5x. Against a name with a 12.02% implied move driven by the first FY27 guide, a new authorisation is a second-order headline.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Put/call open interest ratio of 0.54 is mildly call-heavy, which is the opposite of a chain positioned for a capital-return surprise being pre-bought; but with 1,765 total contracts and a 39%-of-mid ATM spread this is close to noise. The -4.1% five-day run-up gives no sign of anyone front-running an authorisation.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Confirmation that UNFI has already exhausted or formally terminated the 2022 programme, or a company statement deferring capital return until leverage is below 2.0x, would take this near zero.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input verifies and the arithmetic is correct -- FY26 guide $31.1-31.3bn and $2.40-2.60, 39-week actuals of $23,510mm and $1.95, so implied Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn and implied Q4 EPS of $0.45-0.65, with the $0.62 consensus at the 85th percentile. That is the problem. This is a calculation performed on two published numbers -- the company's own narrowed guidance from 2026-06-09 and a consensus print that is, by construction, the price. It requires no non-public input and it is the first calculation any sell-side preview runs. It is also less sharp than it looks. A $0.20-wide implied band around a $0.62 estimate is plus or minus 16%, so 'the 85th percentile' is spurious precision on a quarter where a single item -- fuel recovery, a further insurance recovery, a productivity pull-forward -- swings more than the whole band, and narrowed Q4 ranges are routinely exceeded. And the market has already been taught this lesson the hard way: on 2026-06-09 UNFI missed revenue by roughly $236mm against a $7.96bn consensus, missed EPS $0.77 versus $0.79, merely narrowed rather than raised the guide, and lost 10.28%. Across FY26 the company cut sales guidance from $31.6-32.0bn while raising adjusted EPS from $1.50-2.30 to $2.40-2.60 -- so 'revenue estimates at the guide floor, EPS estimates near the guide top' is not an asymmetry the hunter found, it is the exact residue of a year in which sales guidance came down twice and EPS guidance went up twice, and it is what the -20.9%-from-high, -6.6%-over-20-days tape reflects.

Contemporaneous account of the Q3 print: revenue miss, guidance only narrowed, shares tumble -- the event that re-based revenue expectations to the guide floor.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The consensus is the price by definition. The 2026-06-09 reaction of -10.28% on a revenue miss and a narrowed guide is the tape event that installed exactly this configuration of estimates. Median absolute reaction of 10.18% over 7 prints says the market's uncertainty here is about the FY27 guide, not about whether $0.62 sits at the 60th or 85th percentile of a $0.20 band.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the $0.62 consensus is stale -- e.g. that it was set before the diesel spike and no analyst has revised since 2026-08-13 -- would make the bar genuinely mispriced rather than merely high.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The diesel data is exactly right and I verified it against the EIA series itself: $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 against $3.651 on 2025-08-26, with August 2026 weeks of $5.348, $5.257, $5.454, $5.652, $5.599 versus roughly $3.70 a year earlier. But the target arithmetic that carries the conclusion is factually wrong. The published target is 'Low-double digit average annual growth, ~$800 million target for fiscal 2028' -- the terminal year is FY2028, not FY2027, and there is no published 'FY24 to FY27' EBITDA target to be satisfied. Run it correctly: from the FY24 base of $518mm to ~$800mm in FY28 is about 11.5% a year, whose FY27 waypoint is ~$717mm; and the smooth path from the $695mm FY26 midpoint to $800mm in FY28 is +7.3% a year, i.e. FY27 of about $745mm. So the correct frame gives management cover to guide FY27 in the +3% to +7% range, not flat. Flat at $695mm would require FY28 to jump 15% to hit the published $800mm and would visibly break management's own bridge -- and it would contradict what they told the market on 2026-06-09, which is that FY27 returns to low-single-digit sales growth with improving profitability. The hunter's $690-730mm band happens to brush the bottom of the correct path, so the numerical conclusion is not void, but the 'cover to guide flat' reading is a misreading of the target table. On the priced side: diesel at record August highs is front-page macro, covered by Transport Topics, FleetOwner and Qz through August, published sell-side commentary already names 'fuel costs and transportation expense' as the specific FY27 uncertainty for UNFI, and the tape has been marking it -- $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94 on 2026-09-04. What I concede is magnitude: fuel up ~46% on a $31bn distributor's transportation base is tens of millions against a $695mm EBITDA even after partial recovery, and that scale is not drawn out anywhere I can find.

The actual published target, verbatim: 'Low-double digit average annual growth, ~$800 million target for fiscal 2028' -- fiscal 2028, which is the year the finding misstates as fiscal 2027.
Diesel and gasoline hit record August highs, making the fuel input a headline macro fact rather than an obscure one.
Records seasonal record highs for diesel around $5.40/gal, attributed to constrained global fuel supply.
Published UNFI commentary already flags that competition, promotions, macro pressure, fuel costs and transportation expense add uncertainty to the outlook.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: UNFI went from $47.90 on 2026-08-13 to $43.94 on 2026-09-04 while diesel set records: -4.1% over 5 days and -6.6% over 20 days, with 20d realised vol of 28.8% against 79.5% ATM IV. The fuel fear is visibly in the price on the dates it became known; the residual is magnitude, not existence.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosure of UNFI's annual fuel spend and hedge ratio for FY27 -- with that, the headwind stops being a guess and becomes a number; equally, if the FY27 guide is set at or above $745mm the 'cover to guide flat' premise is dead on arrival. Marked as not reaching this print because the FY27 EBITDA guide, not the Q4 fuel line, is where this resolves, and the target arithmetic that would size it is misstated.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the same claim as UNFI-h1#1 and it is anchored more explicitly on the one document that makes it priced. The 8-K it cites (report date 2026-07-07, filed 2026-07-09) came with exhibit 99.1, a leadership-announcement press release, distributed via Businesswire on 2026-07-09 and picked up within two days by TipRanks, The Shelby Report, Supermarket News, Progressive Grocer, Mass Market Retailers, Abasto and Distribution Strategy Group -- all four of the changes the finding lists (Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10 from Carrier Climate Solutions Americas, Tarditi to President/COO, Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, Bushway's exit) were in the wire copy. The finding's own framing concedes this: it says four of the five were 8-K'd and press-released. The fifth, Echols, I verified is genuinely unpublished outside the Form 4 remark -- I searched and found only his 2022 appointment coverage and the July reorganisation stories, none of which mention a departure. But Chief Corporate Affairs Officer is a communications and public-affairs seat with no P&L, no guidance role and no analyst relationship; treating it as the fact that reprices a name with a 12.02% implied move is a category error. And 'the executive who will deliver the first FY27 guide started five weeks ago' has been knowable, to the day, since 2026-07-09.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No 25-delta skew is computable, so there is no direction statement in the chain to corroborate or refute a governance-risk premium; put/call OI of 0.54 on 1,765 contracts is if anything call-heavy. The July announcement is eight weeks before the print and the 20-day window (-6.6%) does not contain it.

interactions: Four overlaps, and one of them is the most important observation in this pass. (1) UNFI-h1#1 and UNFI-h2#4 are the same claim from two hunters, resting on the same two documents -- the 2026-07-09 8-K/Businesswire release and the 2026-08-27 Echols Form 4. h2#4 is the more accurate and complete version; h1#1 adds only the 'day 29' framing. These must be counted once, and the single unpublished element in both is a corporate-affairs officer's exit with no P&L content. (2) UNFI-h2#0 and UNFI-h2#3 are mirror images on the same variable from the same hunter, pointing in opposite directions: h2#0 argues tiered surcharges make the fuel hit smaller than feared (bullish), h2#3 argues the fuel base makes the first FY27 guide worse than the algorithm (bearish). They cannot both carry full size -- the same surcharge mechanism that rescues Q4 in h2#0 also cushions FY27 in h2#3 -- and netting them leaves far less than the sum. Scoring both at full weight would double-count fuel in opposite signs. (3) UNFI-h1#2 and UNFI-h2#3 both rest on the same one-page target table from the 2025-12-10 investor day release; h1#2 quotes the free cash flow line ('~$300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028') correctly, while h2#3 misstates the adjusted EBITDA line's terminal year as fiscal 2027 when the published target is '~$800 million target for fiscal 2028'. One hunter read the table correctly and one did not, from the same document. (4) UNFI-h1#0 and UNFI-h2#2 are in tension: h1#0's mechanism is a softer top line, while h2#2's own evidence establishes that the sell-side has already marked Q4 revenue ($7.6bn) to the floor of the band implied by guidance ($7.59-7.79bn). h2#2 is therefore the reason h1#0 has little left to deliver. Finally, UNFI-h1#2 and UNFI-h2#2 both draw their numbers from the single 2026-06-09 Q3 FY26 earnings release, which is also the document behind the -10.28% reaction in the history -- four of the nine findings ultimately trace to it.
